methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $65M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Vulcan Elements, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Maslin and Piotr Kulik, has raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public company, including peers such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $65M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding $130M. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector comparables at equivalent or adjacent stages: the median valuation across this set is $1.7B, with a range from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B).

The triangulated valuation range supported by this analysis spans $110M on the conservative end to $2.0B at the high bound, with a median estimate of $915M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate valuation multiples within the frontier robotics sector and the limited precedent for Series A-stage comparable pricing. The peer-median method's reliance on mostly Series B comparables introduces upside bias; the stage-progression floor is mechanically conservative. Resolution of this range will depend on capital efficiency metrics, market traction, and investor appetite for manufacturing automation at this stage.
